# Review of iliad-145 (23.192–286)

Two passes over all 65 units. Pass 1: every grammatical label, every position claim, every cross-reference, notes against their own l and i. Pass 2: Greek to l word by word, l to i, remembered English, quotation marks, and conformity to both house tables and to the published parts. `t` was not touched (checked by script: all 65 `t` identical before and after; the units still cover lines 192–286 once each, in order). Notes re-counted after editing: all between 25 and 110 words, no backticks. No modern translation was opened or recalled; the neighbouring published part (iliad-144) and the packet's repeated lines were read from the repository. gloss.json does not exist yet, so the glosser's parses are not checked here.

Severity: major = a label or sense that is wrong; moderate = departs from a binding table row or a published part, or misattaches a word; minor = polish or precision.

## Findings considered and refused

- 193 ἀλλ’ / ἄλλ’: the source prints ἀλλ’ at 23.193 and ἄλλ’ at 23.140 (checked in the pinned source). The note says exactly this, reads ἄλλ’, and the l and i are the same as the published iliad-144 unit at 140. No change.
- ὀρέοντο as an "imperfect middle": kept in the softened form (see 212). I cannot confirm the exact lemma from memory beyond what iliad-011 and the glossary already say; the label now claims no more than they do.
- ἄλλεγον "built on λέγω": the note says only that it is a verb with doubled λ built on λέγω, the verb of 239. That is true under every account of the form that I know (ἀλλέγω or ἀν-λέγω), so it stands; the glosser should give the lemma and not restate it from the note.
- 198 μετάγγελος "go-between messenger": iliad-092 ships "messenger among" for a dative of the persons she serves; here the dative is the winds she goes to, between Achilles and them. The glossary entry has "go-between, messenger", so l is kept.
- 205 "There is no sitting for me" and the l "No sitting": acceptable; ἕδος is a noun with no verb and the note says so.
- 204 "and spoke a word" (l and i): the Iliad table's 18.391 row has l "spoke a word" and the published 11.647 has i "said"; the published i's for μῦθον ἔειπε vary (iliad-059 "spoke a word to them", iliad-007, -039, -041, -048 "spoke to"). 235 and 271 follow iliad-059. Kept.
- 202 "with their own eyes": the table has "with my own eyes" for ἐσόψομαι ὀφθαλμοῖσι (5.212), so "own" is house practice. Kept.
- 217 "tossing" (l "hurling"): consistent with the notes' βάλλω "throw"; no table row.
- 222 οὗ called "possessive": the genitive of possessive ὅς is οὗ and agrees with παιδός; consistent with the glossary's keeping the possessive apart from the relative. Kept.
- 246 τιθήμεναι "used as a command": the subject Ἀχαιοί is nominative, so an infinitive depending on ἄνωγα (245), which would need an accusative, is the worse reading; the imperatival infinitive stands.
- Speech marks: Iris's speech runs 205–211 and the speech marks are right: “ with the mark on 205, ” at the end of 211. Achilles 236–248: “ at 236 (mark), ” at the end of 248. Achilles 272–286: “ at 272 (mark), ” at the end of 286; iliad-146 begins 287 with ὣς φάτο, so no speech runs on. No change.
- 192 l/i "And"/"Yet": οὐδέ is "and not" and "yet" gives the contrast; no change.
- 212 whole half-line: l and i agree with the shipped pattern of 15.43 / 8.425 (iliad-065, -118); the note's cross-reference to 2.35 is correct.
- 236 repeated line: l and i agree with iliad-044 (the l is identical; the i is the same as the published i up to the cut of the unit). 261 agrees with iliad-055. No Odyssey line of this part is listed in the packet.
- Cross-references checked and correct: 23.140 (ἄλλ’), 23.177 (πυρὸς μένος), 18.352 (ἑανῷ λιτί, iliad-119), 2.35 (ἀπεβήσετο), 9.365 (261 in iliad-055), 239 and 243 (λέγωμεν, φιάλη and δημός), 237–238 and 250–251.
- Unit-boundary claims ("begins in the middle of line …", "ends at the full stop in 257") checked against the lines: correct.

## Second pass (gloss)

Every novel entry in gloss.json (112) and every `__broaden__` entry (24) was checked against the form in units.json: lemma, meaning, parse, Attic equivalent, no line numbers or "here", only the typographic ’, novel entries under 230 characters. All 24 broadened entries are the existing iliad-glossary.json entry whole + " · " + the new reading (verified by script). No form needed a further broadening (ὀρέοντο is already covered: "rose up, hastened").

Changed (16 entries; 12 novel, 4 broadened):
- ἕστατον · moderate · wrongly "plpf. 3 dual … ’the two stood’" → perfect 3 dual with present sense, ’the two stand’ (agrees with l/i of 283).
- ἄλλεγον · moderate · lemma and Attic equivalent: the old "= ἀνέλεγον" cannot be the source of a three-syllable form → ἀναλέγω (epic ἀλλέγω), ἀνα- cut short and assimilated, unaugmented (Attic ἀνέλεγον).
- μεταδαίσομαι · minor · "short-vowel after ἵνα (or fut.)" made exact: short-vowel aor. subjunctive (Attic μεταδαίσωμαι).
- ἐνηέος · minor · "cf. Attic -οῦς" → says what Attic would have.
- λιθέῳ · minor · false "= Attic λίθινος" for an uncontracted -έῳ reworded to give Attic λίθινος as the equivalent word.
- ἑξέτε’ · minor · parse reordered: epic uncontracted ἑξέτεα, elided; Attic ἑξέτη.
- λίπησθε · minor · "general relative clause" was wrong for a future-looking relative with κεν → prospective.
- ἀεθλεύοιμεν · minor · meaning/gloss mismatch: ’we were to hold games’ → ’we were to contend in games’.
- ἀκάχησε · minor · "unaugmented" removed (reduplicated aorist; no Attic equivalent).
- ἐρηρέδαται · minor · "= Attic -νται" impossible for a consonant stem → Attic uses the periphrastic ἐρηρεισμένοι εἰσί.
- ἠρᾶτ’ · minor · "ἠράτο" → ἠρᾶτο.
- θεμείλιά · minor · enclitic-τε accent note added.
- Broadened εὐρύν · minor · "an understood τύμβον" was wrong (τύμβον is expressed in 245; εὐρύν agrees with the pronoun τὸν) → reworded.
- Broadened θύων · minor · new reading ’surging’ → ’raging, surging’ to agree with the unit’s "raging with a swell".
- Broadened σεύαιτο · minor · ’might hurry’ → ’might rush’ (agrees with l).
- Broadened ἵπποισίν · minor · ’to (his) horses’ → ’(in) his horses’ (πέποιθε takes the dative of that in which one trusts).

Considered and kept: πενθείετον (pres. 3 dual, -είετον = Attic πενθεῖτον; subject τώ, so 3rd dual), ῥέζουσ’ (the edition prints the elision; pres. 3 pl., ’they sacrifice’), περιβάλλετον (pres. 3 dual, subject ἵπποι), κεύθωμαι, δεδεγμένα, κεχανδότα, ἑωσφόρος, ἀμφίθετον (sense stated as not known), ἵππον "fem. ’a mare’".
